lab_title: Anatomy and Hemodynamics of the Human Heart
top_level_objectives: Identify the four primary chambers and four valves of the human heart.
Trace the pathway of blood flow through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.
Correlate the physical structure of the left ventricle with its physiological function in systemic circulation.
Understand the mechanical role of heart valves in maintaining unidirectional blood flow.

scenes.brief_purpose: Orient the student to the heart's position in the thoracic cavity and its external landmarks.
key_visuals: Floating 3D model of the heart anchored to the student's desk
Label tags for the major vessels: Aorta, Vena Cava, Pulmonary Trunk
student_actions: Rotate the heart model to identify anterior and posterior surfaces
Touch the vessels to display their names and function

scenes.brief_purpose: Expose the interior of the heart to identify the four chambers.
key_visuals: Color-coded highlights for Right Atrium, Right Ventricle, Left Atrium, Left Ventricle
student_actions: Select each chamber to highlight its boundaries and internal walls
Compare the myocardial wall thickness between the right and left ventricles

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the heart valves and understand their role in preventing backflow.
key_visuals: Magnified view of the Tricuspid, Pulmonary, Mitral, and Aortic valves
Animated demonstration of valve leaflets opening and closing
student_actions: Tap a valve to initiate a 3D animation of a cardiac cycle phase
Observe the cordae tendineae securing the atrioventricular valves

scenes.brief_purpose: Follow the path of deoxygenated blood through the right side of the heart to the lungs.
key_visuals: Flowing blue particles representing deoxygenated blood
Visual path indicators through the Vena Cava, Right Atrium, Tricuspid Valve, Right Ventricle, Pulmonary Valve, and Pulmonary Arteries
student_actions: Initiate the flow sequence to trace blood path
Pause the flow at the pulmonary valve to explain its function

scenes.brief_purpose: Follow the path of oxygenated blood from the lungs, through the left heart, to the systemic circuit.
key_visuals: Flowing red particles representing oxygenated blood
Visual path indicators through Pulmonary Veins, Left Atrium, Mitral Valve, Left Ventricle, Aortic Valve, and Aorta
student_actions: Initiate the flow sequence to trace blood path
Observe the high-pressure ejection into the aorta

scenes.brief_purpose: Assess the student's understanding of structural-functional relationships.
key_visuals: Interactive dashboard displaying labels and clinical scenarios
student_actions: Drag and drop labels to the correct anatomical structures
Answer a prompt explaining why the left ventricle wall is thicker than the right wall
